categories.name: DPS
categories.description: The primary-damage core: hold-to-fire spells that loose a burst then cool down, the player's mirror of an enemy attack.

categories.name: Summon
categories.description: Minions you cast into the fight — they run their own AI and keep working while you move and cast other things.

categories.name: Utility
categories.description: Everything that isn't raw damage or a summon: mobility, buffs, crowd control, denial, and mitigation. Some are instant and layer on top of your damage; others are channeled or charged holds that trade a slot of offence to shape or survive the fight.

spells.name: Pew
spells.description: One burst of single bullets at the cursor, then cooldown, rather than a sustained hose. The burst is short enough to read as a single commitment: you aim and fire, then move on. It is the reliable all-rounder, the spell every other weapon is measured against.

spells.name: Snipe
spells.description: A few homing bullets toward the first enemy in the cursor direction. They all launch on the same frame rather than staggering, so the volley lands as one clustered hit instead of a trickle: a target either eats the whole thing or none of it. Accurate, but low DPS for the cooldown. Use it to pick off a specific enemy, not to clear a room.

spells.name: Blam
spells.description: Two shotgun blasts back-to-back at the cursor, then cooldown: a double barrel, capped at two rather than a sustained run. Both barrels are the whole spell, so a miss on either half is a real cost. It is a close-range shredder: at point blank the two cones overlap almost entirely and the whole pellet count lands on one body.

spells.name: Ring
spells.description: A few fast rings of bullets pulsed out of the caster. Every pulse spawns at the caster's exact centre and expands outward, and each one is rotated off the last, so the gaps between bullets in one ring are covered by the next. There is no aim: the spell is pure area denial around your own body. Walk into a crowd and let the pulses do the sorting.

spells.name: Fireball
spells.description: The starting spell: the first thing a new player has in a slot, and the baseline every other nuke is read against. A homing orb toward the enemy nearest the cursor; it explodes on impact, wall, or max range. All damage is the explosion, so a shot that expires in open air still deals it. The homing and the guaranteed detonation make it hard to waste, which is what a first spell should be.

spells.name: Zaap
spells.description: An instant chain-lightning bolt that leaps between packed enemies; one lone target gets a single zap.

spells.name: Zoing
spells.description: A fast piercing bullet that ricochets off walls; each bounce is a fresh leg of travel and adds damage.

spells.name: Bwoom
spells.description: Charges in front of the caster while held, growing per tick; on release it fires a piercing line whose damage scales with charge.

spells.name: Halp
spells.description: A small squad of ranged minions firing single bullets. A walking gunline.

spells.name: Bzzz
spells.description: A fragile swarm of fast, short-range minions; chaff that dumps damage then dies.

spells.name: Jimmy
spells.description: One heavy minion firing a ring around itself; a walking turret that denies an area.

spells.name: ChargeDash
spells.description: Charges in a direction for a short duration at high speed. Sends bullets at 90 degrees.

spells.name: Thwomp
spells.description: An instant radial knockback pulse; more damage the closer the enemy, chip at the edge. The "get off me" button.

spells.name: Nope
spells.description: On a long cooldown, raises a bubble that absorbs incoming damage; a white ring flashes on each absorbed hit.

spells.name: Heal
spells.description: Instantly restores health. The safety net every survivability loadout considers.

enemies.name: Ash Snake
enemies.description:
Snake variant, and the one that turns a room into a hazard. It flees furthest and fires the
longest, fastest shots of the three, bouncing five times and losing power on each — a volley
that keeps crossing the room long after the snake has gone. Nothing about it is dangerous
up close; everything about it is dangerous a second later.
enemies.blurb: Snake variant, and the one that turns a room into a hazard. It flees furthest and fires the longest, fastest shots of the three, bouncing five times and losing power on each — a volley that keeps crossing the room long after the snake has gone. Nothing about it is dangerous up close; everything about it is dangerous a second later.
enemies.art: the snake recoloured ashen — pale grey-lavender scales with cyan eyes.

enemies.name: Coral Snake
enemies.description:
Snake variant, and the one that corners early. It sees you late and panics at nearly double
the retreat range, so it hits a wall almost immediately and answers with a short-range
shotgun of twice-bouncing shots instead of a lane-filling pair. The trade is the reverse of
the snake's: harmless at distance, a wall of pellets the moment you crowd it.
enemies.blurb: Snake variant, and the one that corners early. It sees you late and panics at nearly double the retreat range, so it hits a wall almost immediately and answers with a short-range shotgun of twice-bouncing shots instead of a lane-filling pair. The trade is the reverse of the snake's: harmless at distance, a wall of pellets the moment you crowd it.
enemies.art: the snake recoloured hot coral — banded orange over red, white eye pixel.

enemies.name: Dirt Golem
enemies.description:
The golem recipe moved into the glade and softened: just as slow, even tougher, but its rings
barely sting. It works as a low-stakes rehearsal for the real golem at the dungeon doors. You
learn to read an area denier that sits still and then lumbers after you, and here a misread is
cheap. You can always outrun it, so the threat is the space it fills.
enemies.blurb: The golem recipe moved into the glade and softened: just as slow, even tougher, but its rings barely sting. It works as a low-stakes rehearsal for the real golem at the dungeon doors. You learn to read an area denier that sits still and then lumbers after you, and here a misread is cheap. You can always outrun it, so the threat is the space it fills.
enemies.art: the golem sprite in packed-earth browns with grass tufts on its shoulders.

enemies.name: Grimling
enemies.description:
Pack hunter. It wanders, then weaves in and fires a three-bolt burst at five tiles, with no
recovery between bursts while you stay in reach. Grimlings share a pack group: one alert —
or one hit — wakes every grimling of any kind in the radius. The weave makes it hard to line
up a shot, and the pack punishes you for focusing one down without a plan for the rest.
enemies.blurb: Pack hunter. It wanders, then weaves in and fires a three-bolt burst at five tiles, with no recovery between bursts while you stay in reach. Grimlings share a pack group: one alert — or one hit — wakes every grimling of any kind in the radius. The weave makes it hard to line up a shot, and the pack punishes you for focusing one down without a plan for the rest.
enemies.art: a small hunched shadow-sprite, gloom-black body with two amber eyes and needle limbs; quick flickering run frames.

enemies.name: Hopper
enemies.description:
A quick closer, and the first enemy that actually comes at you. It `Wander`s until it spots
you, then weaves in and pokes at short range with a fast single shot. Fragile and low-damage
alone; it turns up in pairs with sproutlings, so it teaches you to keep moving while something
crowds your space.
enemies.blurb: A quick closer, and the first enemy that actually comes at you. It `Wander`s until it spots you, then weaves in and pokes at short range with a fast single shot. Fragile and low-damage alone; it turns up in pairs with sproutlings, so it teaches you to keep moving while something crowds your space.
enemies.art: a small round critter with two eyes and stubby legs, glade green (8×8): a two-frame idle and a three-frame hop.

enemies.name: Mandrake
enemies.description:
Low HP, high tempo, always in a pack. Mandrakes uproot and sprint straight at you, wailing a
slow sound wave as they close. One is trivial. The point is the group: three or four converge
so the waves overlap and force you to move. This is the glade's lesson in what the AoE spells
are *for*, and they spawn in exactly the clumps that reward one.
enemies.blurb: Low HP, high tempo, always in a pack. Mandrakes uproot and sprint straight at you, wailing a slow sound wave as they close. One is trivial. The point is the group: three or four converge so the waves overlap and force you to move. This is the glade's lesson in what the AoE spells are *for*, and they spawn in exactly the clumps that reward one.
enemies.art: a root-bodied figure with a screaming face; the wave is two expanding arcs.

enemies.name: Mole
enemies.description:
Introduces the **burrow**. It dives underground where it cannot be hit at all, and the only
tell is a dirt plume tracking toward you; inside three tiles it erupts with a pair of
rotating ring bursts, scratches around on the surface for a beat — your punish window —
then dives again. Fighting it is rhythm reading: move off the plume, hit it while it blinks
in the light.
enemies.blurb: Introduces the **burrow**. It dives underground where it cannot be hit at all, and the only tell is a dirt plume tracking toward you; inside three tiles it erupts with a pair of rotating ring bursts, scratches around on the surface for a beat — your punish window — then dives again. Fighting it is rhythm reading: move off the plume, hit it while it blinks in the light.
enemies.art: a plump maroon-brown mole with oversized pale claws and a pink snout; a travelling dirt-mound sprite while submerged, a burst-of-soil frame on eruption.
enemies.notes: untouchable for the whole burrow (`damage_scale` 0) — the surface beat is the only window.

enemies.name: Moon Moth
enemies.description:
Moth variant, and the one you fight at arm's length. Same flit-in, poke, bolt loop, but the
poke is a pair of scale rings pulsed off its own body, each rotated off the last, so it has
to be right on top of you to land anything. It commits closer than the moth and leaves
sooner. Standing still to trade with one puts you inside the pulse; step off it, not
through it.
enemies.blurb: Moth variant, and the one you fight at arm's length. Same flit-in, poke, bolt loop, but the poke is a pair of scale rings pulsed off its own body, each rotated off the last, so it has to be right on top of you to land anything. It commits closer than the moth and leaves sooner. Standing still to trade with one puts you inside the pulse; step off it, not through it.
enemies.art: the moth recoloured moonlit — pale blue-white wings over a dusk body.
enemies.notes: the shortest attack probe of the three (2 tiles) and the shortest retreat — its poke only works point-blank, so it re-closes fastest.

enemies.name: Moss Golem
enemies.description:
The golem recipe at deepwood weight — the toughest thing in the biome that isn't a boss, and
the slowest. It walks you down, and on arrival it hardens into a shell (a channeled absorb,
the rosebud's trick) that eats whatever you spent punishing the approach; then three rotating
rings pulse out, each turned off the last, dense enough that its own tile is a place you
never stand.
enemies.blurb: The golem recipe at deepwood weight — the toughest thing in the biome that isn't a boss, and the slowest. It walks you down, and on arrival it hardens into a shell (a channeled absorb, the rosebud's trick) that eats whatever you spent punishing the approach; then three rotating rings pulse out, each turned off the last, dense enough that its own tile is a place you never stand.
enemies.art: the golem sprite overgrown: deep-green moss over grey stone, with dim eye-lights; a clenched, hardened frame for the shell.
enemies.notes: the shell is a Nope absorb channelled through the wind-up, so hitting it mid-telegraph is the worst moment to spend a burst.

enemies.name: Moth
enemies.description:
The deepwood's basic flier and its returning face. It flits in on quick wings, pokes twice
with a dust burst at short range, then bolts for a beat before closing again — it never
stands and trades. Always in twos and threes: fragile chip pressure whose job is to keep
you moving while heavier things line up.
enemies.blurb: The deepwood's basic flier and its returning face. It flits in on quick wings, pokes twice with a dust burst at short range, then bolts for a beat before closing again — it never stands and trades. Always in twos and threes: fragile chip pressure whose job is to keep you moving while heavier things line up.
enemies.art: a dusty grey-brown moth with big rounded wings and two pale eye pixels; a two-frame flutter.

enemies.name: Needle Moth
enemies.description:
Moth variant, and the one that taxes the dodge. It strikes from five tiles out and leaves
two homing dust-needles behind it, so its retreat is what buys the shot its time: you are
dealing with the moth that just left while the next one comes in. The needles turn hard but
only over a narrow cone — a sidestep won't shake one, breaking the angle will.
enemies.blurb: Moth variant, and the one that taxes the dodge. It strikes from five tiles out and leaves two homing dust-needles behind it, so its retreat is what buys the shot its time: you are dealing with the moth that just left while the next one comes in. The needles turn hard but only over a narrow cone — a sidestep won't shake one, breaking the angle will.
enemies.art: the moth recoloured rust — tan-orange wings over a dark plum body.
enemies.notes: the longest attack probe of the three (5 tiles) and the longest retreat — it never comes into the range the other two fight at.

enemies.name: Owl
enemies.description:
The perch sniper. It sits still and charges a Bwoom shot at anything inside ten tiles, the
wind-up itself being the telegraph. Get too close, or out of its band, and it repositions a
few tiles before charging again; being cornered mid-reposition just makes it fire. It
outranges most of what you carry at this depth, so your move is to close the gap through
its fire.
enemies.blurb: The perch sniper. It sits still and charges a Bwoom shot at anything inside ten tiles, the wind-up itself being the telegraph. Get too close, or out of its band, and it repositions a few tiles before charging again; being cornered mid-reposition just makes it fire. It outranges most of what you carry at this depth, so your move is to close the gap through its fire.
enemies.art: a brown oval with an oversized head and two big amber eyes. The eye rule taken to a whole creature.

enemies.name: Rosebud
enemies.description:
Rooted like a seedling. `Idle` until you get too close or it takes a hit, then it clamps into
a defensive bud. That bud is a brief high-defence windup that punishes spam-hitting. Then it
blooms into a `RingPattern` whose aim rotates slightly each pulse, and idles again. It teaches
you to read the telegraph instead of face-tanking.
enemies.blurb: Rooted like a seedling. `Idle` until you get too close or it takes a hit, then it clamps into a defensive bud. That bud is a brief high-defence windup that punishes spam-hitting. Then it blooms into a `RingPattern` whose aim rotates slightly each pulse, and idles again. It teaches you to read the telegraph instead of face-tanking.
enemies.art: a closed rose bud on a stem, glade greens with red petals; a petal-spread frame to bloom, a clamped-shut frame for the shell.
enemies.notes: Defensive Shell on the windup: wait out the telegraph, then burn during the bloom.

enemies.name: Seedling
enemies.description:
A sproutling that grew up: the same rooted plant, but instead of one lazy seed it opens into a
slow ring. Where the sproutling teaches that enemies shoot, the seedling teaches you not to
stand next to the thing that shoots. The ring makes its own tile expensive even though it never
chases. It works as area denial, and it stays a speed bump in both glade flavours.

Where the sproutling teaches that enemies shoot, the seedling teaches you not to stand next to the thing that shoots. The ring makes its own tile expensive even though it never chases. It works as area denial, and it stays a speed bump in both glade flavours.
enemies.art: the sproutling sprite crowned with a ring of buds.

enemies.name: Shard Grimling
enemies.description:
Grimling variant, and the pack's back line. It shares the pack, but it stops at nine tiles
and fans a spread of gloom shards instead of closing. On its own the fan is easy to walk out
of; with two of them behind a pack the cones overlap and the gaps you were stepping into
close. The long wind-up is the tell, so the shard grimling is the one you push or break line
of sight on, never the one you trade with at range.
enemies.blurb: Grimling variant, and the pack's back line. It shares the pack, but it stops at nine tiles and fans a spread of gloom shards instead of closing. On its own the fan is easy to walk out of; with two of them behind a pack the cones overlap and the gaps you were stepping into close. The long wind-up is the tell, so the shard grimling is the one you push or break line of sight on, never the one you trade with at range.
enemies.art: the grimling recoloured dark plum, with a duller eye-glow.
enemies.notes: the longest attack probe of the three (9 tiles) and the longest wind-up — it never closes to the range the others fight at, and it keeps firing while they do.

enemies.name: Snake
enemies.description:
A skittish corridor-denier. It wanders until it spots you, then bolts in a random direction;
when its back hits a wall it stands and fires twin parallel shots that ricochet, then bolts
again. Trivial in open rooms; in narrow passages the bouncing pair covers the corridor both
ways.
enemies.blurb: A skittish corridor-denier. It wanders until it spots you, then bolts in a random direction; when its back hits a wall it stands and fires twin parallel shots that ricochet, then bolts again. Trivial in open rooms; in narrow passages the bouncing pair covers the corridor both ways.
enemies.art: a low serpentine coil in deepwood two-tone green, a forked head with a white eye pixel; weave frames.

enemies.name: Sproutling
enemies.description:
Rooted in place, watching. It sits in `Idle` until the player is in sight, then spits a
single slow seed at a steady pace. This is the first enemy the player meets. The seed is slow
enough to sidestep on reflex, so it teaches that enemies shoot without much risk.
enemies.blurb: Rooted in place, watching. It sits in `Idle` until the player is in sight, then spits a single slow seed at a steady pace. This is the first enemy the player meets. The seed is slow enough to sidestep on reflex, so it teaches that enemies shoot without much risk.
enemies.art: a stem, a leaf, and two eyes. The simplest sprite in the biome, in glade green.

enemies.name: Stalker
enemies.description:
The basic pouncer, and the biome's signature jump-scare. It sits in `Disguise` as a scenery
prop, watching through a probe that only reaches five tiles. Step into that — or hit it —
and it reveals, then weaves in and blasts a point-blank shotgun cone with no recovery
between shots. Lose it and it becomes a prop again. Introduces **prop disguise**.
enemies.blurb: The basic pouncer, and the biome's signature jump-scare. It sits in `Disguise` as a scenery prop, watching through a probe that only reaches five tiles. Step into that — or hit it — and it reveals, then weaves in and blasts a point-blank shotgun cone with no recovery between shots. Lose it and it becomes a prop again. Introduces **prop disguise**.
enemies.art: a dark violet-grey cap on a thin stalk with a green leaf flick, indistinguishable from decor until the amber eyes open on reveal.

enemies.name: Thornback
enemies.description:
A charger, introducing the **charge-dash with flank fire**. It runs a long telegraphed
windup, then a straight high-speed dash that sheds bullets off both flanks, then a rooted
recovery that is your punish window. It locks heading at launch and can't corner, so
sidestep the dash and burn it during recovery. Trees are your friend.
enemies.blurb: A charger, introducing the **charge-dash with flank fire**. It runs a long telegraphed windup, then a straight high-speed dash that sheds bullets off both flanks, then a rooted recovery that is your punish window. It locks heading at launch and can't corner, so sidestep the dash and burn it during recovery. Trees are your friend.
enemies.art: a wide squat body, dark-brown armour over a tan body, a spike array along the back.

enemies.name: Thornthrower
enemies.description:
`Wander` until it spots you, then `Chase` until in range, where it fires a single slow homing
thorn that you have to keep moving to outrun. It is cheap pressure that punishes standing still.
enemies.blurb: `Wander` until it spots you, then `Chase` until in range, where it fires a single slow homing thorn that you have to keep moving to outrun. It is cheap pressure that punishes standing still.
enemies.art: an uprooted thorn-plant on root legs, muted glade green with red thorn tips; the missile is a spinning thorn.

enemies.name: Wasp
enemies.description:
A hostile version of the player's Bzzz summon. It flits in on the same flying-minion
behaviour and pesters you with quick stings. Fragile and never a real threat alone. Its job is
to show the summon's logic from the other side, and to drop the spell that turns wasps to your
side. It also appears in the insect deepwood.
enemies.blurb: A hostile version of the player's Bzzz summon. It flits in on the same flying-minion behaviour and pesters you with quick stings. Fragile and never a real threat alone. Its job is to show the summon's logic from the other side, and to drop the spell that turns wasps to your side. It also appears in the insect deepwood.
enemies.art: a small bee in a hostile ochre two-tone (the Bzzz summon recoloured), with eye pixels.

enemies.name: Wisp Grimling
enemies.description:
Grimling variant, and the one that finds you. It sees furthest, runs fastest, and calls from
nearly twice the radius its packmates do, so the first wisp to spot you is what turns a room
into a pack. Its poke is a fast triple flicker at four tiles for almost no damage — the
threat is never the bolt, it's who else is now coming. Kill it first or the fight keeps
recruiting.
enemies.blurb: Grimling variant, and the one that finds you. It sees furthest, runs fastest, and calls from nearly twice the radius its packmates do, so the first wisp to spot you is what turns a room into a pack. Its poke is a fast triple flicker at four tiles for almost no damage — the threat is never the bolt, it's who else is now coming. Kill it first or the fight keeps recruiting.
enemies.art: the grimling recoloured pale — washed lavender body, bright eye-glow; the brightest thing in the gloom.
enemies.notes: pack radius 14 tiles against the grimling's default 8, and the shortest attack probe — it comes all the way in.

enemies.name: Great Owl
enemies.description:
Owl variant: bigger, and its firing band is most of the map — it charges from twenty-four
tiles, further than anything else in the biome can answer. The wind-up is longer and the
telegraph brighter, so the duel stays honest, but it re-perches further away too and the
whole fight is spent closing.
enemies.blurb: Owl variant: bigger, and its firing band is most of the map — it charges from twenty-four tiles, further than anything else in the biome can answer. The wind-up is longer and the telegraph brighter, so the duel stays honest, but it re-perches further away too and the whole fight is spent closing.
enemies.art: the owl sprite enlarged, pale barn-owl white with amber eyes.

enemies.name: Grimlord
enemies.description:
A larger, darker grimling, the pack's alpha, and the one grimling that rolls its beat: a
`PatternPicker` swaps its move at low health rather than adding one. Above a quarter health
it weaves in and sprays five bolts at four tiles. Below it, the spray is gone and it enrages
— seven bolts, faster, from wherever it stands, with no range check at all. On death it
bursts one parting ring. The weave plus the enrage turns the last sliver of its health into
a gauntlet.
enemies.blurb: A larger, darker grimling, the pack's alpha, and the one grimling that rolls its beat: a `PatternPicker` swaps its move at low health rather than adding one. Above a quarter health it weaves in and sprays five bolts at four tiles. Below it, the spray is gone and it enrages — seven bolts, faster, from wherever it stands, with no range check at all. On death it bursts one parting ring. The weave plus the enrage turns the last sliver of its health into a gauntlet.
enemies.art: the grimling silhouette enlarged and near-black, red eye-glow; the enrage frame brightens the eyes.
enemies.notes: enrage replaces the spray below 30% HP; `RingPattern` death burst. Shares the grimling pack group, so it wakes with them.

enemies.name: Mandraker
enemies.description: Rare mandrake that casts fireball
enemies.blurb: Rare mandrake that casts fireball
enemies.art: a root-bodied figure with a screaming face; the wave is two expanding arcs. Palette towards red

enemies.name: Razorback
enemies.description:
Thornback variant: the recovery is gone. Each dash ends in a snap re-aim and a fresh launch,
chaining charge after charge for as long as you stay inside its very long sight line; only a
head-on wall hit stuns it into a real punish window. Fight it near trees and make the forest
do the work.
enemies.blurb: Thornback variant: the recovery is gone. Each dash ends in a snap re-aim and a fresh launch, chaining charge after charge for as long as you stay inside its very long sight line; only a head-on wall hit stuns it into a real punish window. Fight it near trees and make the forest do the work.
enemies.art: the thornback silhouette in near-black armour with red spike tips.

enemies.name: Viper
enemies.description:
The one enemy that runs from you. The instant it sees you it picks a random direction and
slithers off, and it turns to fight only when it can't flee: cornered, it unloads a wide
shotgun barrage and bolts again in a fresh direction. It carries tier-2 gear, so it is worth
chasing. Cut the angle, trap it against a tree, and eat the barrage to claim the drop.
enemies.blurb: The one enemy that runs from you. The instant it sees you it picks a random direction and slithers off, and it turns to fight only when it can't flee: cornered, it unloads a wide shotgun barrage and bolts again in a fresh direction. It carries tier-2 gear, so it is worth chasing. Cut the angle, trap it against a tree, and eat the barrage to claim the drop.
enemies.art: the snake sprite in a rare venom-green with gold banding.

enemies.name: Fae
enemies.description:
The glade's floral capstone. It is a flitting sprite that hangs at range and rolls a fresh
attack each phase on a `PatternPicker`, so the fight never settles into one rhythm. No single
phase is deadly, but each one runs long, so you win by dealing steady damage while avoiding
chip over many cycles.

- **Rings** (`RingPattern`): pulses full rings for several seconds to weave through.
- **Aimed shotgun** (`Volley` + `ShotgunPattern`): a tight cone fired several times in a row.
  Punishes standing still.
- **Rest** (`FaeRest`): does nothing briefly. Your burn window.
- **Chase**: flits straight at you at half your speed without shooting, just to shove you out of
  position. It breaks off and rolls a new phase once it gets close enough.
enemies.blurb: The glade's floral capstone. It is a flitting sprite that hangs at range and rolls a fresh attack each phase on a `PatternPicker`, so the fight never settles into one rhythm. No single phase is deadly, but each one runs long, so you win by dealing steady damage while avoiding chip over many cycles.
enemies.art: a small winged figure, one bright fill and a trail of light (16×16 boss sheet).

enemies.name: Gnarlking
enemies.description:
The apex of the animal deepwood, and the one boss that doesn't roll: it runs ordered `Gate`
ladders, so what it does next is decided by the arena rather than by dice. The fight
alternates two modes and **the player sets the pace of the swap**.

Everything it owns is a close-quarters weapon, and the whole kit is **range-gated** — it
never swings at air. Out of reach it simply walks you down, and distance is a delay, not an
answer.

- **Call → Hunt** *(armoured)*: it rings in a brood of six grimlings — the plain, shard and
  wisp kinds mixed — then comes for you. While any of them stand it takes about a third
  damage, and it works the ladder by distance: **Ground Slam** inside 6 tiles (radial
  shockwave, damage falling off with distance, big knockback — demonstrates **Thwomp**),
  **Shotgun Volley** inside 8, and outside both it **closes**, at a steady advance you can
  outpace but not shake. Chipping the boss here is a poor trade against clearing the pack,
  but not a wasted one.
- **Charge** *(unarmoured)*: the moment the brood is dead — or its 26s life runs out — the
  charge unlocks and the ranged kit drops entirely. The thornback's charge-dash writ large:
  a locked-heading lunge shedding `FlankPattern` bullets. It can't corner.
- **Stalk → second Charge**: after the lunge it prowls for a beat. Still within reach and it
  immediately charges again; broken away and it goes straight to **Winded**. Your footwork
  sets the length of the burst.
- **Stagger**: sidestep a charge into a tree and the head-on slam staggers it — three and a
  half seconds rooted, taking *extra* damage. The fight's best window, and you have to earn it.
- **Winded**: heaves briefly, then calls the next brood.

The decision the loop poses: clear the adds fast and you reach the burn window sooner but
meet the charge sooner too, with the pack's chip damage still on you; ignore them and you
are ground down while the boss walks into your face anyway.
enemies.blurb: The apex of the animal deepwood, and the one boss that doesn't roll: it runs ordered `Gate` ladders, so what it does next is decided by the arena rather than by dice. The fight alternates two modes and **the player sets the pace of the swap**.
enemies.art: a towering forest-lord of bark, antler, and gloom, pale glowing eyes, oversized frame; a rear-and-slam pose for the slam (boss sheet).
enemies.notes: one Thwomp only — no bigger low-HP variant. Below a quarter health it calls three grimlords instead of six grimlings (on a shorter 20s leash), and Winded shrinks from 5s to 3s. `clear_group` on the charge is what makes the brood, not a timer, the phase gate.

enemies.name: Thornmess
enemies.description:
The rooted capstone. It stays on the ground and runs a `PatternPicker`
split into two HP-gated pools. It idles until you are in range, then fires thornthrower
missiles. If you break range it uproots and sprints to close, where it behaves like a rosebud
or fires shotgun volleys. At low health it phase-shifts: it throws spores that fill the screen,
seeds the room with the biome's rooted plants, then returns to the cycle.
enemies.blurb: The rooted capstone. It stays on the ground and runs a `PatternPicker` split into two HP-gated pools. It idles until you are in range, then fires thornthrower missiles. If you break range it uproots and sprints to close, where it behaves like a rosebud or fires shotgun volleys. At low health it phase-shifts: it throws spores that fill the screen, seeds the room with the biome's rooted plants, then returns to the cycle.
enemies.art: a massive tangled thorn-mass with a screaming maw and root legs, glade greens with red thorn tips (boss sheet).
enemies.notes: the low-HP phase swaps in a spore and summon wave rather than layering a summon on top.

families.name: Glade
families.intro: The opening biome, where the player learns the systems and fills out a first kit. Enemy density is low, variety is high, stakes are gentle. It has two sub-biomes: the starting glade, which is pure onboarding, and the veggie glade, which brings in the plant roster and its boss.
families.enemies_intro: The opening biome. It comes in two flavours: the floral **starting glade**, capped by the **fae**, and the rooted **veggie glade**, capped by the **thornmess**.

families.name: Deepwood
families.intro: The second biome, tuned to pressure long-range, squishy builds and push the player into close quarters. Enemies have far more health and hit harder. It is the largest biome in the world — twice the footprint of either glade — and both glades gate into it. The three remaining sub-biomes (mimic, insect, fungal) are proposals; they stay in the ideas section below.
families.enemies_intro: The forest, T3. Eleven natives make up the shared pool meant to appear in every deepwood sub-biome; on top of it the **animal deepwood** adds its own beasts and the **gnarlking**. The whole roster spawns, and the rooms are built to introduce it one mechanic at a time.

biomes.name: Starting glade
biomes.intro: Onboarding: single-enemy rooms first, small mixed groups by T2, then the biome's rare and boss at T3.

biomes.name: Veggie glade
biomes.intro: Brings in the plant roster: thornthrower and rosebud both show up from T1. Groups get denser and harder than the starting glade by T2. T3 keeps the shared rare pair (1x viper, 1x mandraker) and the biome boss.

biomes.name: Deepwood
biomes.intro: One biome in-game, not yet split into the four sub-biomes the design plans. The rooms run a teach-then-test ladder: T0 meets each of the eight mechanics alone in its own room, T1 pairs them off, T2 introduces the six family variations alone and re-tests the pairs, and T3 mixes three kinds at a time around the three rares and the gnarlking. Every enemy has a room of its own, so a run meets all eighteen — the variations are deliberately kept apart, so seeing all three moths or all three snakes means going looking for them.
